case.summary: Case CASE-019 (Card SC-03019-K957): The case involves an account takeover pattern with three affected transactions (4012235, 4012234, 4012232) totaling $789.65 exposure. Real-time risk scoring flagged transaction 4012232 ($521.47) at 0.92 due to billing mismatch [EV-1b30b883]. The card SC-03019-K957 showed elevated velocity with three online transactions in 48 hours [EV-1e9ce4ea] against a historical average of $233.07 [EV-61aa0add]. A new iOS device profile appeared for the first time on this account [EV-a2a1cb1d] and was linked to a prior confirmed fraud case CC-4328 [EV-79bb3f08]. The transaction originated from an anonymous proxy in Argentina [EV-c55e26c3], and the customer denied authorizing the purchases while retaining physical card possession [EV-de09d647]. Prior fraud history includes case CC-4328 for the same customer/card [EV-162f06b2] and a pattern-matched account takeover case [EV-2a0747a3].

sar.narrative: Suspicious Activity Report for CASE-019 documents an account takeover affecting card SC-03019-K957 with three unauthorized transactions totaling $789.65. The investigation was initiated when real-time scoring assigned a 0.92 risk score to transaction 4012232 ($521.47) citing billing address mismatch [EV-1b30b883]. Analysis revealed anomalous velocity: three online transactions occurred within 48 hours [EV-1e9ce4ea], significantly exceeding the card's historical average transaction value of $233.07 [EV-61aa0add]. The transactions were conducted from a previously unseen iOS device profile [EV-a2a1cb1d] that has been associated with a prior confirmed fraud case CC-4328 [EV-79bb3f08]. Network forensics identified an anonymous proxy connection routing through Argentina [EV-c55e26c3], consistent with identity obfuscation tactics. The legitimate cardholder reported no authorization of the disputed transactions and confirmed physical card retention [EV-de09d647]. Historical review shows the same customer/card combination was subject to prior fraud case CC-4328 [EV-162f06b2], and pattern analysis retrieved an additional account takeover precedent [EV-2a0747a3]. The confluence of device anomaly, proxy usage, velocity spike, and cardholder denial supports the fraud determination.
